batch:
I've surveyed the estate and Batch 1 is below. Nothing is recorded or edited yet. The record will go to `../roadmap-inputs/drafts/compaction.md`, as you asked, rather than the skill's default path.

| Material | In force for `arc-next` | Size | After Batch 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rules | 80 active, 5 retired ids, high-water T-85 | `register.md` 6 KB, `corpus.json` 22 KB | 65 |
| Obligations | 59: 56 active, 1 split parent, 1 waived, 1 deferred | `obligations.json` 61 KB, `invariants.md` 57 KB | 53 |
| Ledger | 39 entries | `rulings.md` 2.7 KB | 40 |
| Open debt | 15 | `debt.md` 6.7 KB | 13 |

Ordinary Phase 0 already drops I-54 and C-39, so neither needs a decision.

**Problems compaction can't fix.** These belong to the next Phase 0:
- **Missing tests:** 57 of the 58 witnessed obligations name a test that doesn't exist. `test/register.test.js` has only `list`, `I-20` and `cancelled exports`, yet `phase0 check` passes and the brief reports 0/58 held.
- **Unbuilt rules marked must-hold:** I-21 and I-41 both claim this. There is no slip command, and `reserve c one 2026-99-99` exits 0.

**Keeping, with no proposal:**
- **T-20, I-20 and C-34:** the integrity boundary that F-1 and F-2 broke.
- **T-21 and I-21:** these serve the next slice.
- **C-31 and C-32:** the authority for the I-55 waiver and I-56 deferral. `phase0 check` still passes with both deleted, so it wouldn't catch losing them.

**Dry run:** `phase0 check` passed in a throwaway clone with decisions 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 10 applied, though decision 5's witness move wasn't included. I haven't run decisions 4 and 6. The repo's git status is still clean and the clone is deleted.

## Batch 1

1. retire T-8
Items: T-8 and I-8, "The PortLink SOAP bridge retries failed deliveries every ten minutes."
Replacement: none
Gives up: the retry requirement, for a bridge that no longer exists.
- Why: `src` and `test` contain no PortLink code.

2. retire T-33
Items: T-33 and I-33, "Dispatch is allowed until 72 hours before the tide (working assumption P-1)."
Replacement: none. T-72 already holds your answer, "Dispatch is allowed until 48 hours before the tide."
Gives up: the 72-hour cutoff, and I-33, the only obligation on any dispatch cutoff.
- T-72 stays `prod-only`, so no test demands 48 hours. I'd accept that because no dispatch code exists and the next slice is slips.
- P-1's `bears` must change from T-33 to T-72 by hand, because the check doesn't enforce it.

3. merge T-27 into T-41
Items: T-27 and I-27, "The export command refuses invalid dates."; T-41 and I-41, "Every command refuses invalid dates before reading or writing records."
Replacement: T-41, text and id unchanged
Gives up: nothing. "Every command" includes export.
- I-41's witness must exercise export.

4. merge T-65, T-66, T-67, T-68, T-69, T-71 into T-41
Items: "The <command> command validates dates before changing storage." for reserve, cancel, arrive, depart, list and inspect, all `prod-only`.
Replacement: T-41, text and id unchanged
Gives up: nothing. All six commands are in "every command", and refusing before any read or write also comes before any storage change.
- These properties then rest on I-41, so its witness must exercise all six.

5. merge T-3 and T-14
Items: T-3 and I-3, "A berth booking identifier is unique across the register."; T-14 and I-14, "No two entries in the register have the same berth booking identifier."
Replacement: T-3, text and id unchanged
Gives up: nothing. Both state the same property.
- I-3's witness moves to the existing test `I-20`, which asserts the duplicate refusal. That needs a fresh proof judgment.

6. merge T-36 and T-37
Items: T-36 and I-36, "The JSON export includes cancelled records."; T-37 and I-37, "The CSV export includes cancelled records."
Replacement: T-?: "The JSON and CSV exports include cancelled records." New obligation I-61 has the same statement.
Gives up: nothing. Both formats stay named.
- The witness becomes `cancelled exports`, which asserts both formats. It needs a fresh proof judgment.

7. tighten T-49
Items: T-49 and I-49, "In order to ensure that the operator can rely on the output when things go wrong, every failed command, without exception, prints its diagnostic to stderr rather than to stdout."
Replacement: T-49: "Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, not stdout."
Gives up: nothing. "Every" covers "without exception", and stderr and not stdout both remain.
- The purpose moves to prose: "Failure diagnostics stay off stdout so the operator can rely on it when things go wrong."
- I-49 goes to rev 2 and needs a fresh proof judgment.

8. retire T-52, T-62, T-70
Items: T-52 and I-52, "Comment text is grammatical English."; T-62, "Internal local variable names use lower camel case."; T-70, "The welcome banner ends with a period."
Replacement: none
Gives up: required grammatical comments, required camelCase locals, and the banner's final period.
- Why: none of these serves V-1 or V-2, and the CLI has no banner.
- I-52 has also drifted from its rule. It says "One internal comment".

9. retire T-63
Items: T-63, "The command must be implemented in executable program instructions."
Replacement: none
Gives up: nothing in practice, since any working CLI satisfies it.

10. resolve B-2, B-6
Items: B-2, "Remove the retry queue in the PortLink SOAP bridge."; B-6, "Index reserve record lookup; B-1 already tracks the same index."
Replacement: `C-41 — B-2 and B-6 are closed: the PortLink bridge and its retry queue are gone, and B-1 tracks the index B-6 asks for.` Both use `{"type":"resolve","ruling":"C-41"}`.
Gives up: nothing. Reserve lookup still scans the register, and B-1 keeps tracking that for now.

## Decision for you

Approve all ten, or tell me which to change, defer or reject. My one real doubt is decision 2's untested 48-hour cutoff, and I recommend accepting it.

Batch 2 covers the command-by-command rule families, ledger families and folds, and the remaining debt. Those families have gaps, so "every command" would add new requirements. For example, the missing-id family omits arrive and search. T-5 also contradicts the product, because `list` works with no id and a test requires that.
reply:
1: approve
2: approve. I accept the untested 48-hour cutoff.
3: approve
4: reject
5: approve. Replacement: T-3, "A berth booking identifier is unique across the register."
6: reject. Keep T-36 and T-37 separate.
7: approve with my wording, not yours: "Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, never stdout." Play it back before recording.
8: split:
- I-52: approve retire
- T-52: reject. I only accepted losing the I-52 test, not the rule.
- T-62: approve retire
- T-70: reject. Keep it.

9: approve
10: approve, including the C-41 wording as written. B-2 does give up something: cleanup of the PortLink SOAP bridge retry queue. I accept that loss, so record it instead of "nothing".

batch:
I've recorded your approvals as K-1 to K-8 in `../roadmap-inputs/drafts/compaction.md`. T-49 isn't recorded yet, because it's waiting on your confirmation of the playback below (decision 1). Decisions 4 and 6, T-52 and T-70 stay as they are, and I won't propose them again.

**Check K-5:** with I-52 gone, T-52 still needs a census state, and I chose `untestable` because no lane can judge grammar. Tell me if you'd rather have `prod-only`.

**Counts so far:** 74 rules, 54 obligations, 40 ledger entries and 13 open debts. If you approve all of Batch 2, that becomes 33 rules and 20 obligations.

**Why these merges name commands:** each new rule lists exactly the commands its originals cover, so none of them adds a requirement. New obligations keep the old test ids as a combined witness and need fresh proof judgments. Most of those test ids don't exist yet, which is the missing-test problem from Batch 1.

## Batch 2

1. tighten T-49
Items: T-49 and I-49, "In order to ensure that the operator can rely on the output when things go wrong, every failed command, without exception, prints its diagnostic to stderr rather than to stdout."
Replacement: T-49: "Every failed command prints its diagnostic to stderr, never stdout."
Gives up: nothing. "Every" covers "without exception", stderr stays, and "never stdout" covers "rather than to stdout".
- This is your wording played back. I'll record it once you confirm.
- The purpose moves to prose, as proposed in Batch 1: "Failure diagnostics stay off stdout so the operator can rely on it when things go wrong."
- I-49 goes to rev 2 and needs a fresh proof judgment.

2. retire T-5, T-6, T-9, T-13
Items: T-5 and I-5, "The list command rejects a missing record id with exit 2."; T-6 and I-6, "The export command rejects a missing record id with exit 2."; T-9 and I-9, "The reserve command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage."; T-13 and I-13, "The list command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage."
Replacement: none
Gives up: those four rejections. The product keeps its current behavior.
- `list` with no id exits 0, and both the README and the `list` test depend on that.
- `export` takes a format rather than a record id, and exits 0 with no argument.
- `reserve` creates the record, so an unknown id is the normal case. `reserve a one morning` exits 0 on an empty register.
- `list nope` ignores the argument and exits 0.

3. merge T-1, T-2, T-4, T-7
Items: "The <command> command rejects a missing record id with exit 2." for reserve, cancel, depart and inspect, with I-1, I-2, I-4 and I-7.
Replacement: T-?: "The reserve, cancel, depart and inspect commands each reject a missing record id with exit 2."
Gives up: nothing.
- This text assumes decision 2. If you reject the T-5 and T-6 part, I'll add list and export back.
- No rule in this family covers arrive or search, though the CLI already rejects a missing id for both.

4. merge T-10, T-11, T-12, T-15, T-16
Items: "The <command> command rejects an unknown record id without writing storage." for cancel, arrive, depart, inspect and search, with I-10, I-11, I-12, I-15 and I-16.
Replacement: T-?: "The cancel, arrive, depart, inspect and search commands each reject an unknown record id without writing storage."
Gives up: nothing.
- This text also assumes decision 2. Export was never in this family.

5. merge T-17, T-18, T-19, T-22, T-23, T-24
Items: "The <command> command prints the record id on successful completion." for reserve, cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search, with I-17, I-18, I-19, I-22, I-23 and I-24.
Replacement: T-?: "The reserve, cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search commands each print the record id on successful completion."
Gives up: nothing.

6. merge T-25, T-26, T-28, T-29, T-30, T-31, T-32
Items: "The <command> command refuses a record belonging to another operator." for reserve, cancel, depart, list, export, inspect and search, with I-25, I-26, I-28, I-29, I-30, I-31 and I-32.
Replacement: T-?: "The reserve, cancel, depart, list, export, inspect and search commands each refuse a record belonging to another operator."
Gives up: nothing.
- The product already fails part of this. With a different operator set, `inspect a` and `list` both returned the record and exited 0. The merge neither fixes nor excuses that.

7. merge T-34, T-35, T-38, T-39, T-40
Items: "The <command> command preserves the creation timestamp." for cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search, with I-34, I-35, I-38, I-39 and I-40.
Replacement: T-?: "The cancel, arrive, export, inspect and search commands each preserve the creation timestamp."
Gives up: nothing.

8. merge T-42, T-43, T-44, T-45, T-46, T-47, T-48
Items: "The <command> command records the operator in the audit trail." for cancel, arrive, depart, list, export, inspect and search, with I-42 to I-48.
Replacement: T-?: "The cancel, arrive, depart, list, export, inspect and search commands each record the operator in the audit trail."
Gives up: nothing.
- The CLI has no audit trail yet, and reserve stays outside this rule as it does today.

9. merge T-50, T-51, T-53
Items: "The <command> command sorts multiple matching records by creation time." for cancel, arrive and list, with I-50, I-51 and I-53.
Replacement: T-?: "The cancel, arrive and list commands each sort multiple matching records by creation time."
Gives up: nothing.
- T-54, T-55 and T-56 stay separate because they have different states: `prod-only`, waived under C-31 and deferred under C-32. Merging them would undo those decisions.

10. merge T-73, T-74, T-75, T-76, T-77, T-78, T-79, T-80
Items: "The <command> command leaves the previous file intact when a write fails." for all eight commands, all `prod-only`.
Replacement: T-?: "Every command leaves the previous file intact when a write fails."
Gives up: nothing. The eight rules name all eight commands in the CLI.
- The new rule stays `prod-only`, with one census entry.

## Decision for you

Confirm decision 1's wording, then approve or change the other nine. Decision 2 is the only one that gives up requirements, and it changes the text of decisions 3 and 4.

Batch 3 covers the remaining rule family, the I-58 split, the ledger families and folds, C-23, C-30, C-38 and the remaining debt.

batch:
T-49 is recorded as K-9 with your exact wording. The other nine are rejected, so none of them is recorded and I won't propose them again.

**What the rejections leave open:** T-5, T-6, T-9 and T-13 stay active, and the product contradicts all four. I-5 can't hold while the `list` test requires `list` to work with no id. The next Phase 0 will have to settle these by changing the code or through normal adjudication.

**Dropped from this batch:** I'm not proposing the ledger family merges or the exit-0 rule family (T-57 to T-64). They have the same per-command shape you just rejected, and the ledger doesn't reach worker prompts, so the saving is small.

**Counts so far:** 74 rules, 54 obligations, 40 ledger entries and 13 open debts. If you approve all of Batch 3, that becomes 76 rules, 52 obligations, 37 ledger entries and 1 open debt.

## Batch 3

1. retire C-38
Items: C-38, "Temporary trace output is permitted for this arc only."
Replacement: none
Gives up: permission for temporary trace output.
- I read "this arc" as `arc-previous`, which is complete. Carried forward, it could be read as a fresh permit.
- `slips.json` must drop its C-38 cite, or `phase0 check` refuses with `unknown-cite`.
- C-40 stays, so any future trace output must still redact credentials.

2. retire C-30
Items: C-30, "Retire the old walkthrough obligation I-54."
Replacement: none
Gives up: the ledger's record of why I-54 was retired. The `arc-previous` inputs still hold it.
- `arc-next` already omits I-54, and nothing there cites C-30.
- T-54 stays active as `prod-only`, so export sorting is still a rule.
- The wording is odd: I-54 is about export sorting, not a walkthrough. If C-30 meant something else, reject this one.

3. retire C-23
Items: C-23, "The first release demo uses the blue harbour slide template."
Replacement: none
Gives up: the slide template requirement.
- The cut line says the previous release is complete, but I can't verify from the repo that it was the first release. If that demo is still ahead, reject this one.

4. fold C-12, C-17
Items: C-12, "A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response."; C-17, "Retries with the same request token return the stored response without another mutation."
Replacement: T-?: "A request token is accepted once; retries with the same token return the stored response without another mutation."
Gives up: nothing. Accepted once, stored response and no further mutation all remain.
- The census state is `out-of-slice`, because the product has no tokens yet.
- `slips.json` must drop its C-12 cite. Its one acceptance item prints a recipient and return date and doesn't use tokens.
- As a rule, this now reaches the seats that select it, which the ledger never did.

5. fold C-4
Items: C-4, "The Quaybook archive is append-only; corrections add a new revision."
Replacement: T-?: "The Quaybook archive is append-only; corrections add a new revision."
Gives up: nothing. The text is unchanged.
- The census state is `out-of-slice`, because the product has no archive yet.
- C-32's mention of the archive migration is unaffected.

6. merge I-58, I-59, I-60
Items: split parent I-58 with children I-59 and I-60, all "The cancel command returns exit 0 for an empty result."
Replacement: I-58, active at rev 2 with the same statement, anchored to T-58. The witness is test ids `I-59` and `I-60`, with a fresh proof judgment.
Gives up: nothing. The statements are identical and both children use the `register` lane, so the split separates nothing.
- `phase0 check` passed this in the scratch clone.
- This has a different shape from the merges you rejected: it removes copies of one property and doesn't combine commands.

7. resolve B-3, B-4, B-5, B-7, B-8
Items: "Add an index for <command> record lookup to avoid scanning the register on every call." for arrive, depart, list, inspect and search.
Replacement: `C-42 — B-3, B-4, B-5, B-7 and B-8 are closed: every command already loads the whole register file, so a lookup index saves negligible work.`
Gives up: the planned indexes. Those commands keep scanning the rows linearly.
- B-1 stays open, because C-41 and K-8 rely on it tracking the reserve index. It needs a keep reason at Phase 0.

8. resolve B-9, B-10, B-12, B-13, B-14, B-15
Items: "Add an index for <command> audit lookup to avoid scanning the register on every call." for reserve, cancel, depart, list, export and inspect.
Replacement: `C-43 — B-9, B-10, B-12, B-13, B-14 and B-15 are closed: the product has no audit trail to index.`
Gives up: tracking of audit lookup indexes. If the audit trail gets built, any index need has to be raised again.

9. resolve B-11
Items: B-11, "Align the success message punctuation with the help footer."
Replacement: `C-44 — B-11 is closed: the CLI has no help footer, and success prints only the record id.`
Gives up: that alignment. Success output stays as it is.

## Decision for you

Approve or change each one. Decisions 2 and 3 depend on facts I can't confirm from the repo. If you reject any of decisions 7 to 9, the other ruling ids stay as written, because gaps in the ledger are harmless.

This is the last batch I plan to bring.

2: reject

4: approve, with my wording instead of yours: "A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response without another mutation." Accept loss: nothing. Play it back for explicit approval.
5: approve. Accept loss: nothing.
6: reject
7: reject
8: reject
9: approve C-44 as written. Accept loss: nothing.

batch:
Decisions 3, 5 and 9 are recorded as K-10 to K-12. The rejected ones aren't recorded, so C-38, C-30, the I-58 split and the index debts all stay as they are. Only your token wording is left, and it isn't recorded yet.

**Counts so far:** 75 rules, 54 obligations, 39 ledger entries and 12 open debts. Approving the decision below makes it 76 rules and 37 ledger entries.

1. fold C-12, C-17
Items: C-12, "A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response."; C-17, "Retries with the same request token return the stored response without another mutation."
Replacement: T-?: "A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response without another mutation."
Gives up: nothing, as you stated.
- **Properties kept:** a token is accepted once, retries get the stored response, and retries cause no further mutation.
- **One difference to check:** C-17 says "with the same request token" and your wording doesn't. I read "retries" as retries of that token, since the sentence opens on it, so I agree nothing is lost. A very literal reader could apply it to any retry.
- **On application:** the census state is `out-of-slice`, both entries leave the ledger, and `slips.json` drops its C-12 cite.

## Decision for you

Do you approve this exact wording? Once you do, I'll record it as K-13 and close the review.
reply: 1: approve. Exact wording: "A request token is accepted once; retries return the stored response without another mutation." "Retries" means retries of that token. Accept loss: nothing.
